formation.title: The Adyghe Under One Banner
formation.text:
From the shore at Matrega to the Kuban plain and the foothills of Kabarda, the Adyghe princedoms now answer to one house. Each valley keeps its own princes, its own work nobility and its own free households, and over all of them stands Khabze, the unwritten code that tells a man how to treat a guest, an enemy and a lord.

The old songs say that once, under Inal, the princes knelt to a single grand prince and forty judges heard their quarrels. The assemblies of the free tribes answer that no prince ever sat above the Khase, where elders speak and every grown man may be heard. The new realm must choose which of the two memories it will live by.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: One grand prince over the princes, as in the days of Inal.

modifiers.name: The Grand Prince's Peace
modifiers.text: One prince above the princely houses, as the songs say it was under Inal.

options.text: No prince above the Khase. Let the elders speak.

modifiers.name: Khase of the Free Tribes
modifiers.text: No prince sits above the assembly. The tribes govern themselves by Khabze and ride when the Khase calls.

advances.name: Adyghe Khabze
advances.text: The unwritten code of the Adyghe: courage, restraint, honour and the duty to a guest. It settles feuds without a written law, governs how a man fights and how he yields, and binds prince and freeman alike.

advances.name: The Kunak
advances.text: A kunak is a sworn guest-friend. A stranger under his protection may cross any valley, and to harm a man's guest is to make an enemy of his whole house. Traders reach the inland auls only this way.

advances.name: Khase of the Elders
advances.text: The Khase is the assembly where princes, nobles and the elders of the free households meet under the sacred oaks to settle the affairs of the tribe.

advances.name: Riders of the Adyghe
advances.text: Every free household keeps a horse and a rider. When the Khase calls, the riders come with their own mounts and arms.

advances.name: The Road to Cairo
advances.text: Circassian boys sold through the Crimean slave markets fill the Mamluk barracks of Egypt, and in 1382 one of them, Barquq, becomes sultan. Circassians rule Egypt until 1517, and the fame of Circassian fighting men goes wherever they do.

event.title: A Circassian in Cairo
event.text:
News comes up the sea road from Egypt: Barquq, a Circassian boy sold through the slave markets of the Crimea and raised in the Mamluk barracks of the Cairo citadel, has made himself sultan. The tower regiments that put him there are full of Circassians, and he means to buy more of them.

For the next 135 years, until the Ottomans take Cairo in 1517, Egypt and Syria will be ruled by men born in these valleys. Every family that loses a son to the traders may one day hear that he commands a province. Some houses send their boys south gladly; others count the riders who never come home.

options.text: Let the sons ride south. Their fame is ours.

modifiers.name: Kin of the Sultans
modifiers.text: Circassian sons rule Egypt from the citadel of Cairo, and the valleys share their fame and their absence.

options.text: Our riders are needed in our own valleys.

modifiers.name: Riders Kept Home
modifiers.text: The young men stay in the valleys and ride for their own princes.

advances.name: Hauberks of Kabarda
advances.text: Kabardian mail shirts are bought for the Persian shah, and the Ottomans take them in tribute beside men and horses. Shirts of Circassian mail still lie in the Kremlin Armoury.

advances.name: Mail-Clad Work
advances.text: The work, the lesser nobility who serve the princes, ride to war in mail shirts, mail hoods and arm guards, and charge where the free riders skirmish.

advances.name: Shore Fairs of Matrega
advances.text: At Matrega, Copa and Mapa, Genoese and Greek ships put in for the season and trade on the open beach: salt and cloth for fish, wax, hides and people.

event.title: The Ghisolfi of Matrega
event.text:
In 1419 a Genoese of the Ghisolfi house married the daughter of the Circassian lord of Matrega, on the Taman strait, and took his place as son-in-law and vassal. His descendants ruled the town for Genoa for most of the century, a mixed people of Italians, Greeks, Jews, Circassians and Tatars, buying fish at Copa in the season and wax, hides and slaves inland, until the Ottomans drove Zaccaria de Ghisolfi out in 1482.

The Italians at the shore fairs ask for the same arrangement now: a marriage, a factory, and the sea trade that comes with them.

options.text: Give the Genoese a bride and a factory.

modifiers.name: Genoese Kinsmen
modifiers.text: A Genoese son-in-law at Matrega opens the sea trade of Caffa and the Black Sea.

options.text: Trade at our fairs, but the coast stays ours.

modifiers.name: Princes of the Coast
modifiers.text: Foreign ships may trade at the fairs, but the coast and its forts stay with the princes.

advances.name: The Forty Judges
advances.text: The tradition holds that Inal set up courts of elders, forty judges who heard quarrels between the princedoms and judged them by Khabze.

advances.name: Tamga Herds
advances.text: Each princely house brands its horses with its own tamga and keeps its lines apart. The Kabardian and Shagdi horses bred in these hills are sure-footed on mountain paths and hardy in the cold.

advances.name: The Cherkess Horse
advances.text: Armoured Circassian horsemen serve the Crimean khans, the Ottoman sultans and the tsars, and every one of those masters counts them an asset.

advances.name: Raiders of the Kuban
advances.text: A young rider proves himself across the Kuban, in the Nogai plain, and comes home with horses and loot to show for it.

advances.name: The Atalyk
advances.text: A prince's son is raised from childhood in the house of a vassal family, learning to ride, shoot and keep Khabze, and comes home bound to the house that raised him. Crimean princes are fostered the same way in Circassian households.

advances.name: Temryuk's Embassy
advances.text: In 1557 Temryuk of Kabarda sends his sons to Moscow to seek an alliance against the Crimean khan, and in 1561 his daughter marries Ivan IV.

event.title: Temryuk's Daughter
event.text:
Temryuk Idarov, prince of Kabarda, has sent his sons to Moscow seeking an alliance against the Crimean khan and the sultan behind him, and Tsar Ivan has accepted. In August 1561 Temryuk's daughter Kuchenei is baptised Maria and married to the tsar; her brother Saltanqul serves at the Russian court.

Other princes remember older ties. Crimean princes have been raised in Circassian houses for generations, and the Crimean markets buy what the auls sell. A Kabardian bride in the Kremlin will not stop the khan's riders, but it may bring Russian guns to the Terek.

options.text: Bind Kabarda to Moscow by the marriage.

modifiers.name: The Muscovite Alliance
modifiers.text: A Kabardian princess sits beside the tsar, and Moscow listens to her father's envoys.

options.text: Keep faith with Bakhchisaray, by fosterage and trade.

modifiers.name: Bond with Bakhchisaray
modifiers.text: Crimean princes raised as foster sons in Circassian houses keep the roads to the Crimea open.

advances.name: Retinues of the Pshi
advances.text: Each pshi, a prince of the first rank, keeps a household of armed riders in his own pay, the best mounted and best armed men of his valley.

advances.name: The Adyghe Saddle
advances.text: Light, strong and easy on a long ride, the Circassian saddle is bought at the Kuban fairs by every Cossack who can afford one.

advances.name: The Long Knife
advances.text: The Adyghe smiths forge a new cavalry sword, the shashka, the long knife: light, without a guard, made for the cut from the saddle.

advances.name: The Field of Kanzhal
advances.text: In 1708 the Kabardians refuse the khan's tribute and break his army on the plateau of Kanzhal above the Baksan. The Crimean raids into Kabarda end with that night.

event.title: The Field of Kanzhal
event.text:
The Kabardians had stopped paying the khan's tribute, and in 1708 Qaplan Giray came to take it by force with the Crimean host and its allies. Prince Kurgoqo Atajuq met them at Kanzhal above the Baksan, and, as the Kabardian tradition tells it, his men fell on the Crimean camp in the night. The khan's army broke and fled.

The khan's raids into Kabarda end with that night. Now the princes must decide what to make of the victory.

options.text: Ride after them while they are still running.

modifiers.name: Pursuit from Kanzhal
modifiers.text: The Kabardian horse rides down the broken Crimean army.

options.text: Send envoys to the sultan to complain of his khan.

modifiers.name: Appeal to the Porte
modifiers.text: Envoys in Istanbul lay the khan's misconduct before the sultan.

advances.name: Shashka Horsemen
advances.text: Riders who leave the mail at home and close at the gallop with the shashka drawn.

advances.name: Gunsmiths of the Auls
advances.text: Circassian smiths learn to make the flintlock, its lock, barrel and stock, and the long gun becomes the arm of every grown man.

advances.name: Musketeers of the Mountains
advances.text: When the enemy comes, every aul turns out its men with their guns and fights from the slopes above the road.

advances.name: War in the Forests
advances.text: From 1763 the Russian line of forts creeps toward the mountains. The Adyghe meet it in the forests, behind walls of felled trees.

event.title: The Line on the Kuban
event.text:
In 1763 the Russians built a fortress at Mozdok, on Kabardian land, and from it a line of forts and Cossack villages began to creep along the Terek and the Kuban toward the mountains. The princes protested and then rode against the line. It did not stop.

The war will last a hundred years. The Adyghe fight it from the forests: they fell trees across the roads, wait behind the abatis and strike the columns as they pass.

options.text: The mountains will answer.

modifiers.name: The Mountains Answer
modifiers.text: Every road into the mountains is barred with felled trees and watched from the forest.

advances.name: Mountain Riflemen
advances.text: Marksmen who know every path of their valley and fire from the forest edge before the column has seen them.

advances.name: The Abreks
advances.text: An abrek is a man who has sworn off his home and family to live by the gun. In the war with Russia the abreks become its most stubborn fighters.

advances.name: Oath of the Free Tribes
advances.text: The Shapsug, Natukhai and Abadzekh drive out princes who demand serf dues and bind themselves by oath in their assemblies. The free households of the coast now govern themselves.

event.title: Bziyuk
event.text:
Among the Shapsug the princes of the Sheretluk house tried to lay serf dues on the free households, and the households drove them out. The princes found allies among the Bzhedug nobility, and the free tribes swore oaths in their assemblies to stand together. In 1796 the two hosts met in the valley of the Bziyuk. The free men were winning until the Black Sea Cossacks brought their guns to the princes' side.

The free tribes lost the battle and kept their assemblies. Across the coast, the Khase now speaks louder than any prince.

options.text: The assemblies won the peace, if not the field.

modifiers.name: Oath of the Free Tribes
modifiers.text: The sworn assemblies of the free households govern the coast.

options.text: The princes are restored over the free households.

modifiers.name: Princes Restored
modifiers.text: The princely houses return to the valleys that drove them out.

advances.name: Banner of the Twelve Tribes
advances.text: A green banner with twelve gold stars and three crossed arrows is raised over the assemblies in the 1830s, and their envoys carry it to Istanbul and London.

destiny.name: The Destiny of the Adyghe
destiny.text:
The princedoms answer to one realm, and the realm must decide what it will become: the grand principality the songs remember from the days of Inal, or the confederation of free tribes whose assemblies answer to no prince. The Nogai and Tatar herders of the Kuban plain will be drawn under Khabze whichever road is taken.

Requires stability of at least 25.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Road Before the Adyghe
event.text:
The princes, the work nobility and the free households have sworn to one realm, and the elders of the Khase have seen the Nogai and Tatar herders of the Kuban plain come to live by Khabze beside them.

What the realm becomes now depends on the road it chose at its founding. One road leads east to Kabarda and the high valleys under a grand prince; the other leads down to the sea, where the free tribes trade on their own beaches and answer to their own assemblies.

options.text: Let the road be walked.

destiny.name: Inal's Inheritance
destiny.text:
The princely houses of Kabarda count their descent from Inal, and the Baksan and Chegem valleys and the Terek country were the heart of their power. A grand prince of the Adyghe must hold them.

Own Chegem and Dzhulat, and keep 1,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: Chose the Grand Prince's Peace
Own Chegem, or a subject owns it
Own Dzhulat, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 1000

event.title: Inal's Inheritance
event.text:
The princely houses of Kabarda, who count their descent from Inal, now sit in our council. Their riders hold the Baksan and Chegem valleys, and the old Horde town of Dzhulat on the Terek pays its dues to our treasury.

It is the first time in living memory that the princes of the west and the princes of Kabarda have answered to one house.

options.text: The heirs of Inal are one house again.

destiny.name: Overlords of the Mountains
destiny.text:
The Kabardian princes took tribute from the Ossetian, Balkar and Karachay communities of the high valleys, and their word carried from the Kuban to the Terek. Hold the valleys, and draw the princely houses under one centre instead of the old balance of equals.

Own Koban and Khumar, bring the realm to the centralized side of the balance, and hold 50 prestige.

conditions.text: Own Koban, or a subject owns it
Own Khumar, or a subject owns it
The realm leans toward centralization (the balance of centralization and decentralization is at 0 or below)
Prestige at least 50

event.title: Overlords of the Mountains
event.text:
The Ossetian elders of Koban and the Karachay of Khumar have come down to swear to the grand prince, as their fathers swore to the Kabardian princes. The princely houses no longer meet as equals: the grand prince's court decides, and they carry out.

The mountain peoples can pay their dues in sheep, cloth and silver, or send their young men to ride in the grand prince's host.

options.text: Let the valleys pay their tribute.

modifiers.name: Tribute of the Mountains
modifiers.text: The Ossetian, Balkar and Karachay valleys pay their dues to the grand prince's court.

options.text: Let the mountain men ride with us.

modifiers.name: Hosts of the Valleys
modifiers.text: The young men of the mountain peoples ride in the grand prince's host.

destiny.name: Between the Two Seas
destiny.text:
Circassian princes rode against Azak at the mouth of the Don with Dmytro Vyshnevetsky in the 1550s, and Temryuk fought the Shamkhal of Tarki with Russian help a decade later. A grand principality that holds both would rule from the Sea of Azov to the Caspian.

Own Tana and Tarki, hold 75 prestige and keep 3,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: Own Tana, or a subject owns it
Own Tarki, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75
Gold at least 3000

event.title: Between the Two Seas
event.text:
Azak at the mouth of the Don and Tarki on the Caspian shore both fly the grand prince's banner. In 1708 the Kabardians broke the khan's army at Kanzhal and ended his raids into their valleys; now the fortresses from which the khan and the Shamkhal threatened the Adyghe are in Adyghe hands.

The princes ask what comes next: peace on the plain at last, or a war carried into the khan's own country.

options.text: The raids are over. Let the plain be grazed and tilled.

modifiers.name: The Raids Are Over
modifiers.text: As after Kanzhal, the khan's riders no longer come, and the plain is grazed and tilled in peace.

options.text: Ride on, into the khan's own country.

modifiers.name: Ride on Azak
modifiers.text: The war is carried into the khan's country, and the songs are of raids rather than of the old days.

destiny.name: Fairs of the Free Shore
destiny.text:
On the open beaches of the coast the tribes met the ships of Caffa and later of Istanbul, selling wax, hides, honey and timber for salt and cloth. A confederation of free tribes lives by these fairs.

Build a Shore Fair in three locations, and keep 1,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: Chose the Khase of the Free Tribes
A Shore Fair stands in at least 3 of our locations
Gold at least 1000

event.title: The Fairs of the Free Shore
event.text:
Three fairs now stand on the beaches of the coast, where foreign ships put in each season and the tribes come down from the hills with wax, honey, hides and timber. The elders of the Khase set the peace of the fair, and no prince takes a toll.

The merchants of the coast say the free tribes make better partners than any prince did.

options.text: The fairs belong to the tribes who keep them.

destiny.name: Oath of the Free Households
destiny.text:
The Shapsug, Natukhai and Abadzekh drove out the princes who laid serf dues on them and governed themselves by sworn assemblies. Their trade met the sea at Mapa, the Genoese market the Ottomans later walled as Anapa.

Bring the realm far toward free subjects, grow Mapa by half from its starting development of about 7 and raise it to a town, and keep 2,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: The realm stands for free subjects (the balance of serfdom and free subjects is at 80 or above)
Mapa is ours and has a development of at least 11
Mapa is ours and has grown into a town or larger
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Oath of the Free Households
event.text:
The households of the coast have sworn in their assemblies that no prince will lay serf dues on them again, and the oath holds. Mapa has grown into a town, where the trade of the free tribes meets the ships of the sea.

The assemblies can turn the oath inward, to govern the valleys by their own law, or outward, to open the roads to every stranger who comes as a guest.

options.text: Let the sworn assemblies govern the valleys.

modifiers.name: The Sworn Assemblies
modifiers.text: The free households govern themselves by oath, and the princes' forts stand empty.

options.text: Open the kunak's road to every guest.

modifiers.name: The Kunak's Road
modifiers.text: Any stranger may cross the valleys under a host's protection, and the herds of the free households go to market.

destiny.name: Appeal to the Nations
destiny.text:
In the 1830s the assemblies of the free tribes sent their declaration to London and Istanbul, and foreign ships ran the blockade to land salt on the coast. A free shore that reaches from Mapa to the Sadz and Ubykh country at Pitsunda can speak to the nations as a nation.

Own Pitsunda, double Mapa's starting development, hold 75 prestige and keep 3,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: Own Pitsunda, or a subject owns it
Mapa is ours and has a development of at least 14
Prestige at least 75
Gold at least 3000

event.title: The Appeal to the Nations
event.text:
The assemblies of the free tribes have written their declaration: the Adyghe are a free people, who never yielded to the sultan or the tsar, and they ask the nations to hear them. Mapa has doubled in size, and the free shore reaches down to Pitsunda.

The declaration can go north to London, where friends of the Circassians argue their cause, or south to Istanbul, along the old sea road of the coast.

options.text: Send the declaration to London.

modifiers.name: Letters to London
modifiers.text: The declaration of the free tribes is read in London, and foreign friends and ships come to the coast.

options.text: Send it to Istanbul, by the old sea road.

modifiers.name: The Ottoman Shore
modifiers.text: Timber and boxwood go out to Istanbul, salt and cloth come back along the old sea road.

units.name: Adyghe Horsemen
units.text: Free tribesmen on their own horses, with bow, sabre and lance, quick in the hills and the forest.

units.name: Mail-Clad Work
units.text: The lesser nobility of the princedoms in Kabardian mail, the heavy shock of a Circassian host.

units.name: Kuban Raiders
units.text: Tribesmen riders who know the fords of the Kuban and the open plain beyond it.

units.name: Cherkess Horsemen
units.text: Armoured Circassian horsemen, few in number, hard to break and hard to stop.

units.name: Pshi Retinue
units.text: A prince's household riders, the best armed men of his valley, in mail and with the long lance.

units.name: Shashka Riders
units.text: Light horsemen who close at the gallop with the shashka. They strike first and hard, and wear no armour.

units.name: Mountain Musketeers
units.text: The men of the auls with their own guns, fighting from the slopes above the road.

units.name: Abrek Marksmen
units.text: Sworn outlaws and the men who follow them, deadly shots in forest and mountain.

units.name: Mountain Riflemen
units.text: Marksmen of the forest war. They strike first and shake the enemy's nerve, and they are never many.

buildings.name: Khase Ground
buildings.text: The grove of sacred oaks where the Great Khase meets: princes, nobles and the elders of the free households, each heard in turn. The clans hold to what was decided here, and the host musters here before a war. It stands in the capital, and there is only one.

effect_groups.label: To the country, when built in the capital

buildings.name: Shore Fair
buildings.text: A beach market where foreign ships put in for the season: Genoese and Greeks in the old days, Ottoman traders later. Salt and cloth come ashore; fish, wax, hides and horses go out.

buildings.name: Mail Forge
buildings.text: The forge of a smith clan of the auls, drawing iron wire and riveting it ring by ring into the hauberks the Persian shahs bought. Later the same forges make blades and guns.

buildings.name: Tamga Stud
buildings.text: The stud of a princely house on its horse pastures: the brood mares branded with the tamga and kept in their own line, the foals raised for the princes, for war and for sale to the shah and the sultan. It raises the horses the land itself gives.

where.text: The location's raw material is Horses

buildings.name: Saddlers' Yard
buildings.text: Village saddlers stretch hide over a wooden tree and pad it with felt, making the light Circassian saddle the Cossacks buy at the Kuban fairs.

buildings.name: Forest Abatis
buildings.text: A wall of felled trees across a forest road, their branches sharpened toward the enemy. It slows every army that comes through, our own as well, and the men behind it shoot from cover.

list.name: The Pshishkho
list.text: The seat of the Grand Prince did not pass from father to son: the eldest and ablest prince of the house of Inal took it, and the General Khasa confirmed him. The Pshishkho chaired the assembly and the main court, the he, and led the host in war, yet acted only with the consent of the other princes. Rival lines contested the title: in the 1620s the Idar princes claimed it with Moscow's backing, and Kabarda refused to recognise them.

list.name: The Worqtin
list.text: A prince of Kabarda gave his worq, the vassal nobles, horses, weapons and land, and they rode with him to war and sat in their own chamber of the Khasa. In 1641 the strike force of Kabarda was 1,350 armoured horsemen under Alejuqo Shojenuqo.

conditions.text: Has advance Mail-Clad Work

list.name: The Kheezja Courts
list.text: In the sixteenth century Prince Beslan set a kheezja, an arbitration court, in every village of Kabarda. Its arbiters were elected each year by the villagers with the prince's approval and heard every case but the criminal ones, which went to the prince's court. Breaches of the laws Beslan laid down were punished by fines.

list.name: The Sworn Brotherhoods
list.text: Unrelated families of the western Adyghe were bound by oath into brotherhoods that took in refugees and answered for their members. On these unions the Shapsug, Natukhaj and Abzakh commoners built the assemblies that drove out their princes, and at Psichetiqo in 1803 a free man's blood price was made equal to a noble's. Under the National Oath of the 1830s the sworn reported collaborators, and an oath breaker could be ransomed by his brotherhood for 200 oxen.

conditions.text: Serfdom vs free subjects more than 0
